_about: The city objects palette (docs/design/city-objects-plan.md 3.2). Step 1 (solid classes) starts it with the classes alone: one row per class of collider face, the answer the car gets (H hard, S smash, P push, R ride, G ghost) and a note. Every class answers H in step 1, which is today's behaviour. Step 4 adds planned: the answer the research gives the class (docs/design/drivable-city.md 3: fences and hedges smash, parked cars are pushed, platforms are ridden over; walls by height and ground guard rails by what is behind them, here their hard default), shown by the collider view (--colliders, game/scripts/collider_view.gd); nothing else reads it. Step 2 adds the barrier types (types, see _types). game/scripts/solidity.gd reads it; map_builder.gd _solid and the dressing scripts' bodies name these ids (game/tools/check_solids.gd).

_types: Step 2 (the wall builder): one row per barrier type, today's looks, read by game/scripts/solidity.gd (types, type_row) and drawn by game/scripts/city_barriers.gd. id; family (heavy, light, low; nothing reads it yet: the later steps' panels and breaking); draw (slab: a box along the line, _wall_along; railing: posts and two rails you see through, _railing_along, on an upstand of `upstand` m in `colour`, posts and rails in `rail`, a post every `posts` m, every `posts_mapped` m on a line OpenStreetMap maps the fence type or a ball-stop net of; city_wall, guard_rail: their own builders); colour (hex, the body); thickness and height (m; height is the default when the line has no mapped `h`); h_range: a mapped height clamped to it; low_height, low_thickness: a mapped wall that low is that thin; material: the OSM `m` (tools/barrier_tags.py) whose colour, and unmapped height, the row gives a wall; placed: a street pass (game/data/road_objects.json), the bake's `st` (tools/object_fixes.py) or city_barriers.gd SITE_WALLS may name it, and an OSM line kind named so is drawn with it; note.

_looks: W2 of the walls look (docs/design/walls-true-to-life.md 6.1-6.3): one row per barrier line type (`ty`, tools/object_types.py TYPES), the rows of the walls doc 6.2, read by game/scripts/solidity.gd (looks, look_row) and drawn by game/scripts/city_barriers.gd when barrier_look is not classic. barrier_look picks the look the city is drawn in: classic (the `types` rows, today's drawing, bit for bit: the default until F has looked at another on the phone) or typed (W2: these rows) or panels (W4: typed, with the `panel` rows as instanced panels); `--barriers=classic|typed|panels` overrides it for a run of the runtime city and for tools/bake_city.gd (the prebuilt city is the look it was baked in, map/sectors/city.stamp). Only a line whose style chain in city_barriers.gd ends at its kind's own row (or what _mapped_style made of it) is drawn from its row; every placed, hand-picked or site look stays classic. A typed look is a `looks` row; the `types` rows are the classic look and are not edited for it. W4 (walls doc 6.4): under barrier_look panels, a row marked `panel` is drawn as instanced 2 m panels with their own shader (city_barriers.gd panel_along, map_builder.gd Panels, game/shaders/panel.gdshader, its numbers packed by game/scripts/panel_rule.gd); every other row draws as typed; its colliders are the typed ones. Keys: id (the ty); family (light breaks, heavy stops, low is ridden over; ghost: not drawn); panel (W4: true, drawn as panels under barrier_look panels; W5: every light row but rail_tram, and stadium_fence, a keep row, is panels under panels only, its gates as ever); draw (rail: posts, rails and a foot, city_barriers.gd rail_lite_along; slab: a box along the line, wall_along, at thick; keep: drawn by the classic chain whatever the look; none: not drawn); h (m: the height when the line has neither OSM's h nor the bake's hs); h_range (OSM's h or hs clamped to it); thick (m); colour (sRGB hex); alt ([[colour, share], ...]: that share of the lines, by a hash of the line's stable id); post ({every m, w m, colour: absent for the row's colour; in_mesh (W5): under panels the posts stay in the city mesh as typed draws them, the panels hold what is between}); rails (0, 1 or 2: one under the top, a second 0.35 m over the foot); foot ({h, colour} or, heavy rows, {h, darken}; W2 draws a foot under a rail row, 0.2 m thick); read by later phases (W4 to W9) and written here so that the look is decided once: open (the share you see through), bars (m between bars), ribs, leaf (W5: a leafy row's leaves, the share 1 - open of its fill), top (flat, sag, leafy: W5 draws them, panel.gdshader), broken (walls doc 7: down, torn, gap, flat, stub, notch, none), debris (metal, wood, sheet, leaf), cap ({h, over, colour, alt, lighten}; parapet_concrete: its upstand and rail), bay ({len, step, post_w, proud, post_colour}), pier ({every, w}), top_rail, marks; note. W7 (walls doc 6.5, the heavy kit, city_barriers.gd wall_kit) draws a heavy or low slab row's foot (h, darken: a band of the face that much darker), cap (h, over: a coping that much wider each side, in colour, or alt with the line's alt colour, or the line's colour lighten that much; over 0: a band of the face, a noise screen's pale top; upstand: the solid part's height, a rail of rail_colour on posts every rail_post_every m to h over it), bay (len m, every other one step darker; post_w: a post that wide at each bay's joint, proud m (default 0.03) out of each face, in post_colour or the line's colour darkened 0.1), pier ({every, w, colour}: a pier w m square every that many m, rising 0.15 m over the top; on a light row (bars_pier) on its foot's plinth (foot thick, default 0.3), with a diamond collider on a soft line), top_rail ({colour, h, hz}: a rail h over the wall's top on posts every 2 m where the line's hazard reason is in hz); a run's ends get a pier or a post where the row has them, else end faces.

_debris: W6 of the walls look (docs/design/walls-true-to-life.md 7): the colour of what a broken panel throws, by its looks row's `debris` (game/scripts/solidity.gd debris_of, debris_colour; soft_things.gd's burst). metal, wood and leaf are the colours the bursts had before W6 (soft_things.gd's old table: metal, wood, hedge); sheet is new (building-site hoarding: light galvanised sheet). A line whose type has no `debris` throws by its kind as before W6: leaf for a hedge, wood for a board fence, metal for the rest. The sound is picked by the same word (main.gd _on_soft_broke: leaf the hedge's, wood the wooden fence's, metal and sheet the metal fence's).
